statement: Let \(\overline{ab}\) be a two-digit number. A positive integer \(n\) is a relative of \(\overline{ab}\) if: the units digit of \(n\) is \(b\), and the remaining (nonzero) digits of \(n\) sum to \(a\). Find all two-digit numbers that divide all of their relatives.

Let \(ABC\) be a right triangle with right angle at \(A\) and \(AB < AC\). \(M\) is the midpoint of \(BC\) and \(D\) is the intersection of \(AC\) with the perpendicular to \(BC\) through \(M\). \(E\) is the intersection of the parallel to \(AC\) through \(M\) with the perpendicular to \(BD\) through \(B\). Show that \(\triangle AEM \sim \triangle MCA\) if and only if \(\angle ABC = 60^\circ\).
Let \(n > 1\) be an integer. In how many ways can the numbers \(1, 2, \ldots, 2n\) be placed in a \(2 \times n\) grid, one per cell, so that any two consecutive numbers are in cells sharing a side?

For which positive integers \(n\) can an \(n\)-step staircase figure be covered by \(n\) squares of integer side lengths, not necessarily equal, without overlapping and without extending beyond the staircase?

Let \(ABC\) be an acute triangle with altitudes \(AD, BE, CF\). The circle with diameter \(AD\) intersects \(AB\) and \(AC\) at \(M\) and \(N\) respectively. Let \(P, Q\) be the intersections of \(AD\) with \(EF\) and \(MN\) respectively. Show that \(Q\) is the midpoint of \(PD\).

Let \(n\) be the sum of the digits of a natural number \(A\). Call \(A\) 'surtido' if every integer from 1 to \(n\) can be expressed as a sum of (distinct) digits of \(A\). (a) Prove that if \(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8\) are sums of digits of \(A\), then \(A\) is surtido. (b) If \(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7\) are sums of digits of \(A\), must \(A\) be surtido?
